subject: Treating subject as a random effect to run multiple mediation

messages.author: 52048a95197bc226
messages.subject: Treating subject as a random effect to run multiple mediation
parts:
Hello, I've used the lavaan package to run a multiple mediation model with four mediating variables. However, each subject ran three trials of the task so I need to treat subject as a random effect. Is there a way to incorporate this into the lavaan analysis? Would I just add +(1|Subject) to each regression in the model?
Thanks!

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Treating subject as a random effect to run multiple mediation
parts:
I would treat each of the trials as a variable or maybe with lavaan.survey, treating subject as a cluster. . Hard to say exactly how without knowing more about your study. 

Jeremy

messages.author: 52048a95197bc226
messages.subject: Re: Treating subject as a random effect to run multiple mediation
parts: I'm not seeing any documentation for using the piecewiseSEM package for a multiple mediation model. Our study was online with 100 subjects. Each subject ran three trials of the task (randomly assigned to levels of each IV). We are not interested in making any comparisons between subjects, we just need to make sure that our effects aren't due to any subject differences, so I was told to treat subject as a random effect.

messages.author: 253141a6efac547e
messages.subject: Re: Treating subject as a random effect to run multiple mediation
parts:
Right. Within piecewiseSEM, you can fit models with random subject effects. See the example on the github page https://github.com/jslefche/piecewiseSEM taken from Shipley’s paper with multiple random effects. You might also be interested in http://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01845

If there is a way to do this in lavaan, I’d love to know about it! You can use lavaan.survey to do conceptually similar things,which might be appropriate for the kind of data you have.
